The current low-level goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the parent high-level goal (HLG) of 'Ensure transparent and traceable product sourcing'. Each LLG represents a distinct, documented functional interaction or effect that supports the customer in making informed purchasing decisions. The LLGs include viewing product origin details, browsing and comparing farmer offers, placing orders with minimum quantity constraints, modifying orders due to availability issues using precedence and fair-play rules, reviewing and accepting modified orders, and canceling orders when all products are unavailable with notification.

The LLGs are supported by documentary evidence in the source description. They accurately reflect the system's capabilities without redundancy or omission. The parent HLG is fully realized through these children, adhering to the specified actor criterion of document-supported automatic effects that do not require a manual trigger by the customer actor.

No unsupported or misleading LLGs were identified. All essential documented parent capabilities have corresponding children, and there are no differences in wording or presentation that would justify regeneration.
